messages:
alex.sre: incident-bot alerted ~10:12 UTC about rising 429/502 on /v1/generate from eu-west-1. noticed a step-change at ~10:08.
incident-bot: [P2] Increased 429 rate observed on inference-api (eu-west-1). Top affected routes: /v1/generate, /v1/embeddings. Paging: #eng-oncall.
deploy-bot: deploy 2026.03.15-627 succeeded to canary in eu-west-1 at 10:05 UTC (sha abc123).
jordan.oncall: I can take first look. grabbing graphs. can everyone mute notifications here and update only critical notes? :ear: 10:13
maya.infra: looking at autoscaler logs — a few worker pools hit max queued requests 10:07-10:10. queue depth + KV-cache misses jumped for long requests.
lee-pm: any customer-visible errors reported yet? support says a handful of 502/429 tickets from two tenants in EU. no outage page yet.
alex.sre: customers reporting timeouts -> HTTP 502 and 429 throttles. initial triage: traffic spike from one large tenant + a new model canary that increases per-request tokenization time.
jordan.oncall: reproduced in dev: when request size > 2k tokens latency spikes and triggers backlog. looks like small window where continuous batching pooled long requests and killed throughput.
maya.infra: metrics: 429 rate 5.3% over last 5m (baseline 0.1%), 502s ~0.8%. RT 95p for /v1/generate from eu-west-1 jumped to 2.1s -> 8.7s.
alex.sre: mitigation options: 1) apply per-tenant QPS cap (quick); 2) route traffic to other regions for affected tenants (requires route change); 3) disable canary model variant (if model change is root cause); 4) temporary global request-size limit.
jordan.oncall: I'm going to apply a targeted tenant QPS cap for tenant:alpha-analytics (suspected) to 20 qps. will notify support and set for 15m with auto-remove.
lee-pm: please post the support wording so we can craft a short note.
jordan.oncall: posting: "We're seeing elevated throttles for some requests in EU. We've applied a temporary per-tenant rate cap for alpha-analytics to protect platform stability. If you're seeing errors, reply here and we'll coordinate."
maya.infra: applied tenant cap for alpha-analytics -> 20 qps at 10:20 UTC. tracer: rt-filter shows immediate drop in queue depth.
alex.sre: good. next: I'm flipping the canary model off in eu-west-1 while we observe. will initiate rollback command.
alex.sre: rolling back model variant canary -> command: `redwoodctl rollout cancel model/canary-eu-west-1 --force`
deploy-bot: rollback job started (job id 27619). estimated completion 2m.
incidence: small follow-up — watch dashboard panels: /dashboards/429-503-eu-west (link) and /dashboards/pooling-queue-depth (link).
jordan.oncall: metrics after cap + rollback: 429s down to 1.2% in 2m; 502s steady at 0.6%. RT95 trending back to 3.4s. still above baseline but improving.
maya.infra: also enabled prefix KV-cache warming for model family X (temporary) to reduce cache misses; pushed config via infra-config at 10:23. note: warming increases memory but reduces cold latencies.
lee-pm: are any customers still impacted? support: two open tickets (alpha-analytics resolved), one partner (beta-apps) still reporting intermittent 502s.
jordan.oncall: reaching out to beta-apps now; in parallel I'll keep the tenant cap on for another 10m and watch.
alex.sre: suggestion: add a transient smoothing alert to avoid noisy paging — set 429 alert to fire only if >2% over 3 consecutive 1m buckets. will file a post-incident action.
maya.infra: agree. also adding a dashboard annotation at 10:20: "targeted tenant cap + model rollback" for correlation.
jordan.oncall: handoff: I'll stay until 11:00 UTC. if things look stable by 10:40, I'll drop the cap to 30qps then remove. tagging oncall-next: @alex.sre for second monitor after 10:55.
alex.sre: ack. I'll take over at 10:55. leaving notes: suspect interaction between continuous batching + large token requests + new canary model exec path. ACTIONS: A1 rollback canary (done), A2 tenant cap applied (done), A3 KV-cache warm-up (done), A4 short-term alert smoothing (queued).
deploy-bot: rollback job completed at 10:22 UTC (job id 27619).
lee-pm: support wants a short statement for customers: "We've applied temporary protections to stabilize inference in EU; services should be returning to normal. We're monitoring and will follow up if further action is needed." can we send that?
alex.sre: fine to send. add: "If you continue to see throttles, send logs and request IDs to support."
jordan.oncall: small update at 10:35: 429s now 0.6%, 502s 0.4%. RT95 2.8s. closing loop with beta-apps — they saw a few improved requests after KV-warm.
maya.infra: keeping autoscaler shims active. will revert KV-warm in 30m.
alex.sre: note for postmortem: add runbook gap: need per-tenant gradual backoff rather than blunt caps, and automated model-canary throttles when request-size distribution shifts.
jordan.oncall: handing off to alex.sre at 10:55 UTC. leaving this channel for non-urgent updates.
alex.sre: taking over. will monitor until 11:20. if anyone sees regression ping me directly. :white_check_mark:
incidence-bot: thread marked resolved for paging, but monitoring continues.
lee-pm: thanks team — will prepare customer follow-up and a short RCA draft.
(ends)
